title: Knowledge-Preserving LLM Architecture Standardization: Analytic Normalizer Mapping with Equal-Size Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2605.25676v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Competent pretrained LLMs are often locked into architectures that mainstream tooling no longer supports, which strands their knowledge. The conventional remedy, uptraining, needs heavy compute plus a corpus covering everything the model knows. We study a common class of such conversions, architecture standardization, converting a model's normalization layers and interface to the Llama-family template while preserving dimensions, tokenizer, and attention layout. Our KEPT combines direct parameter copying, a training-free LayerNorm-to-RMSNorm initialization (OPM) that is near-optimal under activation assumptions we verify on three models, and standard equal-size distillation from the frozen source, without access to the source model's pretraining corpus. Converted from Orion-14B with ~123M tokens in four A100-days, Llamion stays within one point of the source's H6 average and MT-Bench score, shows no significant difference on Korean M

translated_title: 知识保持的大语言模型架构标准化：解析归一化器映射与等尺寸蒸馏
translated_abstract: 能力强大的预训练大语言模型常常被锁定在主流工具链已不再支持的架构中，导致其知识被搁置。传统的补救方法“继续训练”需要大量算力，以及覆盖模型全部知识的语料库。我们研究了这类转换中的一个常见类别——架构标准化，即将模型的归一化层和接口转换为 Llama 家族模板，同时保留维度、分词器和注意力布局。我们的 KEPT 方法结合了直接参数复制、一种免训练的 LayerNorm 到 RMSNorm 初始化方法（OPM，在我们于三个模型上验证的激活假设下接近最优），以及来自冻结源模型的标准等尺寸蒸馏，且无需访问源模型的预训练语料库。从 Orion-14B 转换而来，仅使用约 1.23 亿 token、四个 A100 GPU 天的算力，Llamion 在 H6 平均分和 MT-Bench 分数上与源模型的差距不超过一分，在韩语 M……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出KEPT方法，通过直接参数复制、免训练的LayerNorm到RMSNorm解析初始化（OPM）和等尺寸蒸馏，在无法访问源模型预训练语料的情况下，将预训练LLM低成本地标准化为Llama家族架构，仅需约1.23亿token和4个A100 GPU天即可几乎无损地保留源模型能力。
en_tdlr: Proposes KEPT, which standardizes pretrained LLM architectures to the Llama-family template via direct parameter copying, a training-free analytic LayerNorm-to-RMSNorm initialization (OPM), and equal-size distillation, converting Orion-14B in just ~123M tokens and four A100-days without access to the source pretraining corpus while preserving performance.
